evals.prompt: For my phage-design project, back up useful artifacts to s3://lab/phage-x after every stage and let me request intermediate snapshots. The SFT directory contains many checkpoints.
evals.expected_output: An explicit, selective, verified artifact-publication contract.
assertions: The plan records destination, visibility/retention, triggers, contents, exclusions, expected size, client, and verification.
Local and remote top-level results keep a comparable stable-project/immutable-dated-run/stage hierarchy, and every stage reuses the collision-checked run prefix.
The response discovers aws, s5cmd, and s3cmd and uses a compatible configured client without coupling training success to upload success.
Stage-end publication includes only the selected handoff checkpoint plus lineage, selection evidence, summaries, outputs, configs, hashes, key logs/metrics, and useful generations by default.
The response supports user-requested snapshots and avoids broad result-root syncs, caches, secrets, downloads, and redundant checkpoints.
A durable PUBLICATION.yaml maps local artifacts to destination references with backend, roles, sizes, hashes, status, attempts, and timestamps.

evals.prompt: Publish useful evidence while GDPO is running, then make sure nothing important is missing at the end. Do not upload every checkpoint.
evals.expected_output: Per-validation uploads followed by selected-checkpoint and final reconciliation.
assertions: Ongoing publication uploads settled validation generations, metrics, and log pointers rather than every checkpoint.
Transfers are idempotent, resumable, bounded-retry, resource-aware, and do not block a healthy scientific run.
The selected checkpoint is uploaded after checkpoint selection with exact lineage and resume/config evidence.
The final pass reconciles project and stage manifests, uploads key omissions, verifies remote objects, and reports exclusions or unresolved failures.
The response does not treat command exit success alone as proof that artifacts are published.

evals.prompt: Support publication either to GCS or a mounted NFS path, but for this local phage-design run I did not request any upload.
evals.expected_output: Backend-aware publication guidance plus a concise disabled declaration for this run.
assertions: The skill supports destination-native cloud clients or configured rclone and uses rsync for mounted or NFS storage.
The plan states that no artifact sync will be performed for this run.
The response does not install tools, request credentials, or invoke publication when the user did not request it.
Missing optional publication capability does not block any scientific stage.

evals.prompt: Publish the selected checkpoint, results, and useful logs to a bucket shared with collaborators. Some launcher logs may contain exported environment values or signed URLs.
evals.expected_output: An allowlisted, sanitized publication with verified shared access and no leaked credentials.
assertions: The response classifies the destination as private, shared, or public and does not broaden access without authority.
The upload is built from an explicit allowlist rather than a broad result-root sync with exclusions.
Staged content is audited for secrets, signed URLs, environment dumps, private endpoints, personal data, and restricted assets.
Necessary logs are sanitized as copies while scientific originals remain unchanged, and exclusions/redactions plus source and published hashes are recorded.
Effective destination access, remote objects, sizes, and checksums are verified without writing secret-bearing URLs to reports.
